# READ ME FIRST


**NOTE ABOUT SOUND LEVELS (LUFS)**:

- "Normalising" will raise (or reduce) the inbound audio level based on the loudest moment in all of it. This makes it the best level control at this stage without effecting the sound (compression, eq, expanding, reverb, and all that stuff, leave all that to post production imo).

- I set ambient levels to about -40 LUFs, dialogue audio to -23 or -16 LUFS, depending on level I want. For a guide, Spotify forces all audio to -14 LUFS, but you want to leave some headroom for post-production and to be sure to avoid clipping, so I dont go above -16 LUFS and lean into -23 more often.  

**ISSUES WITH LIPSYNC WHEN DRIVEN BY AUDIO OF DIALOGUE THAT HAS A LOT OF SILENT MOMENTS**:

- oddly so far at lower res (960 x 402) it hasnt been an issue so this stage tends to work and is less important than the next workflow for driving lipsync.

- LTX 2.3 I find using audio in often doesnt work for lipsync and the mouth wont move if there isnt a lot of audio dialogue. The trick is to add ambient audio in to the full length just room or environment sound (see the audio merge node, adjust LUFS to get levels, use "mean" to blend the two audio files - dialogue and ambient, but watch out for clipping, also you dont want the ambient audio driving action, just enough volume to not be dead silence). 

- This wasnt needed in LTX 2. but is needed in LTX 2.3. I downloaded 10 seconds of room ambience from freesound.org. You dont have to add it to the resulting video and it doesnt have to be audible, just something that is getting rid of the absolute silence should work. If you have a lot of dialogue then it usually isnt needed. - Mark, May 2026.

## 1. ISSUES TO BE AWARE OF

- **Over-complexity will start to fail.** I could not get 4 people working well when x5 actions were needed. after +50 runs I got it working once (changing other settings it changed again). Ironically it worked in a workflow where I pasted the prompt relay text into a normal text encode. so Prompt Relay wasnt even involved when it worked !!!! I then used that seed and eventually got an end result through the upscaling samplers, which was another story. But it was a fight. </br>

- **Seeds will make a difference** and also every sampler it goes through during the upscale process later (v2v), will change everything again even if you use the same seed it wont help. Bear this mind.</br>

- **Try disabling ALL the Loras if you are fighting something**, I realised loras are not trained on 4 people and that caused issues when I was trying to drive 5 different actions across those 4 people it kept cloning action onto different characters that I wasnt asking for. NAG didnt stop it nor seed changes.</br>

- **Give every person just one action only, try to avoid people having no actions or multiple actions are different times**. A problem I gave myself was having the black woman speak twice and the woman on the far left never speak. This presented issues I never solved but got lucky (50:1 goes before I got a result that could not be repeated).

## 2. GENERIC PROMPT RELAY BEST PRACTICES

***IMPORTANT NOTE: this is my current thinking and purely anectdotal, not an official method***

**This example prompt worked well (came from a guy called "N0NSens" on discord channel), analyse its structure to understand best practice.**:

**global prompt**: `Static camera shows a black woman in a leopard print dress, a man in jeans, a woman in a blue dress, and a woman in black pants and a leather vest (left) are chatting near an elevator in a hotel lobby. All characters are standing and remain where they are.`

**main prompt**: `The black woman in the leopard print dress says seriously, "Okay, let's count. I'm first," and looks at the man in jeans. | The man in jeans cheerfully says, "Okay, I'm second," and glances at the woman in the blue dress. | The woman in the blue dress says calmly, "Well, then I'll be third," and thoughtfully examines her manicure. | The woman in black pants and a leather vest (on the left) says disappointedly, "Well, of course! And I'm naturally last..." She frustratedly puts her hand to her forehead and shakes her head in disapproval.`

- **The structure is “micro-scene scripting”. Each clause is:**

	- One character
	- One emotional adverb
	- One line of dialogue
	- One physical cue
	- One camera implication
	
- **Adverbs are doing the heavy lifting. Adverbs are controlling the emotional performance:**
*Rule of thumb: Use one adverb per character action. More than one creates noise.*

	- seriously
	- cheerfully
	- calmly
	- disappointedly
	- frustratedly
	
- **Verbs define intention and prevent unwanted motion.**:
*These verbs are static-intent verbs, not locomotion verbs. Rule of thumb: Use static verbs when you want the scene to stay still.*

	- looks at
	- glances at
	- examines
	- puts her hand to her forehead
	- shakes her head

# WHAT IS THIS WORKFLOW FOR

i2v this is where I first make video idea from a single image.

- I use this workflow to create structure as quickly as possible and test changes to the prompt quickly. Once I have it at low res (480 up to 960 on long edge depending on what I am doing) and doing what I want it to then... </br>

- Next, I take the result to the  v2v dual-upscaler workflow where I try to keep the structure in tact, but improve the quality and detail to 1920 on the long edge.
